_comment: Manifest of the ECC-provided surface. Nothing here is vendored.
role: Supplies the bulk of the running skill and command catalog.

skills.installed_as: copied by the ECC installer - real directories, not junctions
skills.note: Largest single component. Counting these plus the 5 authored skills in .agents/skills/ and the 64 under ~/.agents/skills gives the catalog. See docs/skills-catalog.md for routing.

commands.note: ECC ships a large command set. The 6 operational slash commands this workbench depends on (/verify /doctor /stack /refresh /re /state) are defined in config/opencode.jsonc.template instead, so they survive an ECC update.

plugins.note: index.ts is intentionally INERT. OpenCode auto-loads every file in plugins/ AND the ./plugins config entry, so a barrel that registered hooks would initialise each hook twice. It must still be a valid v2 definition or the loader marks it failed and the TUI shows it red.

hooks.note: hooks.json carries only keys the harness accepts. $schema, id and description live in hooks.metadata.json because Claude Code reports any other key as unknown at load time.

local_adaptations.ecc-v2-shim/ecc-hooks.ts: Ported to the OpenCode v2 plugin shape. Re-applied after every pull with a timestamped backup.
local_adaptations.ecc-v2-shim/index.ts: Inert v2 entry point. Re-applied after every pull.
local_adaptations.scripts/update-ecc.ps1: pull -> npm install -> build -> install-apply --profile full --enable-hooks, then re-apply the two v2 files, strip the legacy "plugin": ["./plugins"] key, audit only {file:...} references, then run ecc.js doctor and opencode plugin list. opencode.jsonc is never touched.

excluded_from_this_repo: The 315 skills and 103 commands themselves - affaan-m/ECC content, MIT, reproduced by running the installer rather than copied.
LLM-jailbreak prompt agents in agents/ (DeepSeek, GEMINI, GLM and Muse variants). Not workbench methodology.
A live-format credential that was present in service.json.
Two DayZ project handoff documents - that project has its own repository.
